experiments.name: dependent chain with add.d restore
experiments.notes: Dividend 0x7fffffff, divisor 3: a wide quotient with a non-zero remainder. The result is restored to the dividend by adding back (dividend - remainder), so 1 cycle of add.d is subtracted.

latencies.notes: Data-dependent (rj-chained). Measured over 400 dividend/divisor pairs. Min 5 cycles at dividend=0, divisor=2; max 22 at dividend=0x7fffffff, divisor=1. The sample experiment uses the max-latency pair; add.d helper latency (1 cycle) is subtracted.

throughput.notes: Data-dependent throughput. CPI 3.5 at dividend=0, divisor=2; CPI 12 at dividend=2147483647, divisor=1. Measured with 8 independent lanes.

notes: Latency model: 5 cycles with a zero dividend or quotient, otherwise 7 + floor(quotient_bits/2) for the 32-bit form, up to 22 cycles. The remainder path exits early when the remainder is zero, so the divisor-1 recipes used for the divide do not reach the long path here. On LA464 the 32-bit forms also require properly sign-extended operands in their 64-bit registers: a register holding 0x00000000ffffffff instead of 0xffffffffffffffff divides as a tiny value, returns 0 and takes the fast path.
